R6 fires on `except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError): return None` wrapping `parse_interpretation_requirements(existing_options)`.

TIER. `existing_options` is the STORED component's options mapping, Tier-3 by this tree's own declaration: `_requirements` (web/interpretation_state.py) carries `@trust_boundary(tier=3, source="NodeSpec.options['interpretation_requirements'] ... an untyped Mapping[str, Any] entry persisted on composer state and round-tripped through sessions.db storage, a composer LLM tool call, or YAML import")`, and `parse_interpretation_requirements` is that boundary's public accessor. Its docstring declares its failure vocabulary verbatim -- `KeyError` / `TypeError` / `ValueError` on any malformed row -- so the three caught types are that vocabulary named exactly, not a bare `except Exception`.

WHAT THE FUNCTION COMPUTES. Identity CONTINUITY, not admission. Its docstring is "Return one unambiguous trusted current ID for an auto-staged kind", and it already returns None for two other entirely non-exceptional reasons: no stored requirement of that kind, and more than one (`matching_ids[0] if len(matching_ids) == 1 else None`). A stored row the accessor refuses to parse is the same fact as an ambiguous one -- no unambiguous trusted id is available. `None` is the function's declared outcome for "cannot determine", which is why the R6 structural test (a default-valued return counts as silent) fires on a branch that hides nothing.

WHAT THE SWALLOW COSTS. Nothing an admission gate depends on. The single consumer is `_options_with_pending_requirement`, which uses the value only to overwrite the freshly minted requirement's id (`requirement = {**requirement, "id": trusted_id}`). On `None` the requirement keeps the deterministic id its stager already computed -- `_prompt_template_review_requirement_id` (`prompt_template_review:<node_id>`), `_model_choice_review_requirement_id` (`model_choice_review:<node_id>`), or `_source_review_requirement_id` (tools/sources.py). Replacement inside `_options_with_pending_requirement` is keyed on `replace_kind`, never on the id, so the pending row is still replaced exactly once: the swallow path produces no orphaned row and no duplicate row, only a requirement whose id is the canonical computed one rather than the one an unreadable stored mapping happened to carry.

CONTROLS THAT MAKE THE SWALLOW SAFE, BY SYMBOL. Enumerated over every reachable path, not sampled. `_trusted_requirement_id_for_kind` is reached only through `_options_with_pending_requirement`, whose three stagers are `_options_with_default_prompt_template_review` and `_options_with_default_model_choice_review` (both behind the composite `_options_with_default_llm_reviews`) and `_options_with_source_blob_review` (tools/sources.py).
  (a) `_options_with_default_llm_reviews` has five call sites. Four pass a real `existing_options` and every one of them runs `_canonical_interpretation_requirement_error` on the STAGED result immediately afterwards, rejecting the whole write with error_code `interpretation_requirements_invalid` unless every row is the exact canonical field set with exact-str id/kind/user_term/status: `_execute_upsert_node`, `_execute_patch_node_options` and `_prepare_transform_candidate` (tools/transforms.py), and `build_set_pipeline_candidate` (tools/sessions.py), which additionally runs `authored_node_interpretation_requirement_parse_error` on the same staged options. The fifth, `composition_state_from_runtime_yaml` (web/composer/yaml_importer.py), passes NO `existing_options` at all, so `_trusted_requirement_id_for_kind` returns at its first statement (`if existing_options is None: return None`) and the flagged handler is UNREACHABLE from the YAML-import path.
  (b) `_options_with_source_blob_review` has two reachable paths, and both run `_canonical_interpretation_requirement_error` on the staged options before the source is accepted: `_resolve_source_blob` (tools/sources.py), and the inline-blob branch of `build_set_pipeline_candidate` (tools/sessions.py) through its `_options_with_inline_blob_source_review` wrapper.
  (c) Upstream of all of these the authored delta was already gated by `_resolver_owned_interpretation_requirement_error`, and in the guided lane `_interpretation_requirements_malformed_error` (tools/sessions.py) parses through the same `parse_interpretation_requirements` and converts a refusal into a recoverable candidate failure the planner repair loop can act on.
So a corrupt stored mapping is reported by the canonical gate on the way out on every path where it can be observed at all, while this helper -- whose only job is recovering an id -- correctly abstains.

WHY NOT RE-RAISE. These helpers run inside the composer tool / candidate_finalizer seam where an unprefixed exception is a TERMINAL failure. Re-raising would convert every subsequent edit of a node whose stored requirements are already corrupt into a 500 instead of a message-bearing, recoverable tool rejection -- the defect class elspeth-bceffeba19 that the validator-returns-a-verdict shape across this module exists to prevent. Nor can the finding be cleared by returning a non-default value the way `_normalize_trusted_legacy_interpretation_requirements` does two functions down (`return options` in the same handler shape): that function's meaningful "no change" answer happens to be its input, whereas this function's declared return type is `str | None` and `None` IS the answer. Spelling it as anything else purely to move the finding would be semantic distortion.
